events.reader:
Selected audience: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Situation context (grounded; check applicability): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.
events.reader_segment: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does
events.promise: Resend gives this engineer a documented way to route authentication email through a provider they choose, with paid plans that do not impose a daily Resend sending limit, while leaving the hosted authentication platform’s separate rate-limit setting under their control.
events.arc: In one email, move the reader from recognizing that upgrading a hosted authentication plan does not necessarily change its built-in email limits to seeing Resend as a concrete custom-SMTP option they can evaluate through the Supabase-specific setup guide.

emails.job: Get a noncustomer who owns authentication email to assess Resend as the custom SMTP provider for that flow.
emails.single_idea: Resend is available as a custom SMTP path for authentication email: paid Resend plans remove Resend’s daily sending cap, but the engineer must still configure SMTP and adjust the hosted authentication platform’s separate rate limit.
emails.objection: Switching the sender behind a live authentication flow could become a project the engineer does not have time to absorb.
must_not_say: Do not promise that Resend changes, bypasses, or automatically adjusts Supabase’s own rate limit.
Do not promise that Resend detects or survives an upstream dashboard action that clears SMTP configuration.
Do not claim the Free plan removes daily limits; it is capped at 100 emails per day and 3,000 per month.
Do not describe Raycast’s 30-minute waitlist-email test as a complete migration or a guaranteed setup time.
Do not claim transactional and marketing traffic are isolated by account or infrastructure; both can exist on Resend, and IP isolation requires an eligible Scale-plan dedicated IP.
Do not claim Resend explains how Supabase counts sends against its limits.
Do not introduce broad superiority claims about speed, integration breadth, quality, effort, control, security, or deliverability.
Do not turn the announcement into a list of Broadcasts, Automations, Templates, dedicated IPs, compliance credentials, or enterprise features.
Do not state or imply that every reader uses Supabase. Present this integration conditionally (for example, 'If you use Supabase...') unless the user-supplied campaign context establishes it.

Resend is a separate provider, not a change to the auth platform's own limiter: the platform's dashboard rate limit still has to be raised by hand after wiring SMTP, and Resend's own free tier reimposes a 100-emails-a-day cap.

Only the paid tiers remove the daily cap; on the free plan the engineer swaps one 100/day ceiling for another, and nothing in the ledger speaks to the auth platform's own rate-limit setting that still has to be raised.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: The hosted platform’s subscription tier and its built-in email provider limit are separate concerns; upgrading the former does not itself provide a new SMTP sender or raise the latter.
emails.mechanism: Resend provides Supabase-specific SMTP instructions and credentials. After connecting them in Supabase Authentication settings, the engineer separately raises Supabase’s initial 30-message-per-hour custom-SMTP limit. Resend Pro has no daily email limit, while the Free plan remains capped at 100 emails per day.
emails.call_to_action: Read the Supabase SMTP setup guide — https://resend.com/docs/send-with-supabase-smtp
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Resend can serve as the custom SMTP provider for the product’s Supabase authentication email.
emails.next_step_value: The guide shows the Resend SMTP credentials and the Supabase configuration path needed to assess the integration.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading and following the guide does not raise Supabase’s separate rate limit automatically, prove production deliverability, or establish that a complete migration will take 30 minutes.

events.body:
You can now use Resend as the custom SMTP provider for authentication email. Resend is a transactional email platform for developers, with a documented setup path for Supabase Auth.

If you use Supabase, connect your Resend SMTP credentials under Authentication, Email, then SMTP Settings. This changes the sender behind signup confirmations, password resets, invites, magic links, and OTPs.

Supabase’s rate limit remains a separate setting. After configuring custom SMTP, raise its initial **30-message-per-hour** limit under Authentication, then Rate Limits; upgrading the Supabase plan alone does not configure a new SMTP sender.

Resend Pro has **no daily email limit**. The Free plan remains capped at 100 emails per day.

The guide shows the credentials and Supabase configuration path needed to assess the integration.

events.preview_text: Route authentication email through Resend while keeping Supabase’s rate limit under your control.
events.body:
If Supabase Auth returns a 429, checking the Auth logs can confirm where the request failed. It still leaves you to configure a custom SMTP sender and manage Supabase’s separate rate limit.

We’re launching Resend, a transactional email platform developers can use as the custom SMTP sender behind authentication flows.

The Supabase guide shows where to copy your Resend SMTP credentials and add them under Authentication settings. After saving them, you separately adjust Supabase’s initial **30-messages-per-hour** custom-SMTP limit under Authentication > Rate Limits.

Resend Pro has **no daily email limit**. The Free plan remains capped at 100 emails per day, so the Resend plan and Supabase rate-limit setting should be assessed separately.

The guide provides the credentials and configuration path needed to decide whether Resend fits your authentication email flow.

readers.persona:
Selected audience (explicit constraints): The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Context (grounded; applicability must be checked): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.
Source: https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/34209; quote: I am experiencing an issue where authentication emails (magic links/OTP) are blocked with a 429: email rate limit exceeded error, even though I have not exceeded the email limits.
Source: https://github.com/orgs/supabase/discussions/35315; quote: I'm encountering a persistent 429 (Too Many Requests) error with the message AuthApiError: email rate limit exceeded when calling supabase.auth.signUp from my React frontend application.
Problem context: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.; source: https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/34209
Problem context: Upgrading the platform's paid subscription tier does not raise the built-in email rate limit; only configuring a separate custom SMTP provider does.; source: https://github.com/orgs/supabase/discussions/35286
Problem context: An unrelated dashboard action (creating or deleting an Auth Hook) silently wipes the custom SMTP configuration and resets the email rate limit back to a low default, with no warning shown in the UI, and the effect on real auth email only becomes visible later.; source: https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/49873
Problem context: It is unclear to the reporter how the platform counts emails and API calls toward its documented rate limit, since the observed failure point does not match the documented threshold.; source: https://github.com/orgs/supabase/discussions/29167
Problem context: Mixing transactional and marketing email sending on the same provider/domain creates a deliverability risk: a marketing-driven spam complaint or unsubscribe spike can get the account suspended and take down transactional (auth-critical) sending with it.; source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=41594209
Problem context: A homegrown transactional-email setup (enums, templates, tracking) that starts simple for signup/password-reset grows into an unwieldy system as a SaaS product and its users grow, without anyone wanting to fully outsource it.; source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=21486289
readers.what_it_sells: Resend is a transactional email service I can configure as Supabase Auth’s custom SMTP sender, moving signup, reset, invite, magic-link, and OTP delivery off Supabase’s built-in sender while I still manage Supabase’s separate rate limit.
readers.biggest_doubt: The email tells me how to connect Resend and what it costs, but not what operational work follows—domain verification, deliverability setup, monitoring, failure handling, or how safely I can test and roll back—so I cannot yet judge whether this reduces my burden or merely moves it.
